summary: Simulator for a demand-aware queue with multiple producer versions and branching ancestry.

traps.quote: Operation `i` creates version `i` from earlier version `b`; versions may branch. N,Q <= 150000
traps.consequence: Materializing complete O(N)-sized snapshots for all Q versions requires O(Q×N) memory, exceeding limits.
traps.guard: Reconstruct version state from operation ancestry on demand; do not store full snapshots.

traps.quote: `r` is unique integer in `0..1000000006` congruent to signed value modulo 1000000007.
traps.consequence: Using x % MOD directly for negative x produces negative r, yielding wrong hash values.
traps.guard: Use formula ((x % MOD) + MOD) % MOD to ensure r stays in [0, MOD).

traps.quote: N one-shot producers and queue tickets `0..N-1`. ... Producer IDs are `1..N`.
traps.consequence: Confusing 1-indexed producer IDs with 0-indexed tickets causes off-by-one errors in slot access.
traps.guard: Keep producer IDs 1-indexed; queue and tickets 0-indexed; translate carefully at each use.

traps.quote: Unpublished slot stops draining. Value consumed only if `d>0`; then `c` advances. If `d=0`, stops before.
traps.consequence: Checking demand before unpublished, or merging rules, consumes values that should block draining.
traps.guard: Check unpublished first (immediate stop); only for values, test d>0; stop before consuming if d=0.

traps.quote: COMPLETE if `p=c=N`; WAITING if `c=p<N`; BLOCKED if `c<p` unpublished; BACKPRESSURE if value d=0.
traps.consequence: Checking status conditions out of listed order or merging them outputs wrong status strings.
traps.guard: Determine status by checking conditions in order; halt at first match (COMPLETE → WAITING → BLOCKED → BACKPRESSURE).

traps.quote: For every `P`, print: `DRAIN m h status p c d` using the resulting state.
traps.consequence: Wrong token order, leading zeros in numbers, or omitted fields causes all outputs to fail token comparison.
traps.guard: Print one space-separated line per drain: DRAIN m h status p c d with numbers unpadded in decimal.

input_shape: N producers and Q operations. Each operation creates a version from an earlier base version, with commands to reserve producers, publish values, add demand, or drain the queue.
output_shape: For each drain operation: one line with token count, hash, status, and final state (p c d).
invariants: Producer IDs are 1-indexed (1..N); queue tickets and indices are 0-indexed (0..N-1).
Versions form a DAG; each operation builds from an earlier version, possibly branching.
Drain consumes slots in order starting at c, stopping on unpublished or (value with d=0).
max_scale: N=150000, Q=150000, each operation O(N) state; demand up to 10^18.
